skill.description: Check AI video prompts for unclear camera movement, conflicting motions, missing pacing, and incomplete framing before generation. Get a score and specific suggestions for revision.
skill.summary: Review camera movement and framing in AI video prompts before generating a clip.

content.user_title: Check Camera Movement in AI Video Prompts
content.value_statement: Unclear camera directions can waste video generation credits on clips that miss the intended shot. Check the wording before generation and get specific changes to improve movement, pacing, and framing.
actual_capabilities: Detects supported camera terms such as dolly, pan, orbit, and static camera.
Flags ambiguous zoom wording, unlabeled dolly and zoom combinations, and three or more competing movement axes.
Flags missing pacing cues and vague adjectives without concrete speed or timing.
Checks for starting framing or a subject or horizon anchor, and for an explicit final frame.
Returns a score out of 100, a status, and revision suggestions for each flagged rule.
Produces Markdown or JSON reports locally and omits the full prompt by default.
limitations: Uses fixed text patterns that can miss unusual wording or treat sequential moves as competing movements.
Does not generate video, inspect footage, or verify how a specific video model will interpret a prompt.
Does not build storyboards or plan transitions between keyframes.
A passing score measures wording against the rules. It does not guarantee the intended result.

use_cases.title: Clarify a first shot
use_cases.description: Check whether a draft names a camera move, keeps the subject framed, and specifies where the shot ends.

use_cases.title: Diagnose unwanted camera motion
use_cases.description: Review wording from a failed clip for conflicting moves or a mismatch between physical travel and lens zoom.

use_cases.title: Review a shot list before generation
use_cases.description: Check each shot separately and use the rule codes to prioritize revisions before spending generation credits.

prompt_templates.title: Check one prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this camera prompt: [prompt]. Tell me the score and the first change I should make.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first review of a short video prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a zoom
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this shot: [prompt]. I want the camera to move toward the subject. Flag lens zoom wording and suggest a minimal revision.
prompt_templates.scenario: A shot should show perspective changing as the camera approaches.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve competing moves
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this shot for competing movement axes: [prompt]. Keep [primary move] and [subject framing]. Suggest a pacing cue and a final frame, then check the revision.
prompt_templates.scenario: A single shot contains several camera directions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two shot revisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these two camera prompts separately: [draft A] and [draft B]. Compare their scores and rule codes. Recommend which one better preserves [intended movement and final composition].
prompt_templates.scenario: Two drafts express the same shot with different camera instructions.

output_examples.input: Cinematic zoom in on the watchmaker.
output_examples.output: 10 out of 100. High risk of an unclear shot. Choose between a physical dolly and an optical zoom. Specify pacing, starting framing or an anchor, and the final frame.

output_examples.input: Start from a medium shot. Slowly dolly in toward the watchmaker, keeping the horizon level. Settle into a close-up and hold steady.
output_examples.output: 100 out of 100. Pass. The prompt specifies a dolly, a slow pace, starting framing, a level horizon, and a held close-up.

best_practices: Check one shot at a time so the linter does not group movement terms from separate shots.
Specify the main movement, its speed, and what should stay in frame as the camera moves.
Describe where the camera ends and check the prompt again after revising it.
anti_patterns: Using the word zoom when you mean that the camera physically moves closer.
Adding more camera movements to a single shot without a clear primary move.
Relying on adjectives such as cinematic instead of specifying speed and a final frame.

faq.question: Which video generators can I write prompts for?
faq.answer: The same wording checks can review prompts intended for Runway, Kling, Sora, Veo, or Seedance. The linter does not connect to these services.

faq.question: Does the linter need an API key?
faq.answer: No. The linter runs locally with Python and uses no external packages or API calls.

faq.question: What score counts as a pass?
faq.answer: A score of 85 or higher passes. That score reflects the wording checks, not the quality of a generated clip.

faq.question: Can I check multiple shots at once?
faq.answer: Review each shot separately. The linter applies its movement checks to all the text in each input.

faq.question: Does it automatically rewrite my prompt?
faq.answer: The linter provides revision suggestions. It does not automatically replace your prompt or create a storyboard.

faq.question: Will my full prompt appear in the report?
faq.answer: The full prompt is omitted by default, but matched camera terms can appear. The optional prompt display setting includes the prompt text.
